BOUNDARY: The proof correctly restricts to \(n\ge 1\) (required for Heine‑Borel and the coordinate bound). The range is non‑empty, so the boundedness definition yields a centre \(q\) and radius \(r>0\). The constructed \(M=r+\|q\|_2\) is positive, guaranteeing the box \(Q\) satisfies \(a_k=-M\le M=b_k\); thus Heine‑Borel applies. The extension to any norm on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) follows from norm equivalence (the constants preserve boundedness and convergence). The case \(n=1\) is consistent with the one‑dimensional theorem via the isometric identification of \(\mathbb{R}\) with \(\mathbb{R}^1\). No choice principle is used, as advertised.

SOURCES: Every supplied cited item was inspected. The critical dependencies – boundedness definition (def‑metric‑bounded‑diameter), coordinate inequality (lem‑every‑norm‑on‑rn‑is‑continuous‑for‑the‑euclidean‑metric cl. 3), compactness of closed boxes (thm‑heine‑borel‑rn cl. 1), the ZF implication “compact \(\Rightarrow\) sequentially compact” (thm‑compact‑implies‑the‑other‑compactness‑forms), and the subspace metric (def‑isometry‑and‑metric‑embedding) – each supports the exact claim made in the proof step that cites it. No mismatch in hypotheses, quantifiers, or boundary conventions was found.
